identification.summary: Microsoft tracks Storm-2697 as a financially motivated actor that operates The Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) platform while affiliates conduct the intrusions [S1]. The Gentlemen encryptor is written in Go, obfuscated with Garble, targets Windows, and uses double extortion [S1]. Sophos CTU tracks the group behind the scheme as GOLD SHERWOOD [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: emerged around mid-2025 as a closed group and began offering the RaaS to affiliates in September 2025 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-2697 (financially motivated) [S6]. MITRE tracks the group as The Gentlemen (G1058) and lists Storm-2697 and GOLD SHERWOOD as associated names [S5]. Sophos reports that the first victims appeared on the leak site in September 2025 [S2].

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor is identified in the cited sources. Microsoft describes the operators as financially motivated [S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft names Storm-2697 as the operator of the RaaS platform; this is a vendor tracking designation, not a government attribution [S1]. Sophos attributes the scheme to GOLD SHERWOOD [S2]. Equivalence of the Microsoft and Sophos clusters is stated by MITRE [S5] and is not independently verified here.
attribution.basis: Microsoft analysis of the encryptor and observed attacks [S1]; Sophos CTU analysis of 15 intrusions [S2]; ESET reporting on the group's centralized EDR-killer tooling [S3]; Check Point Research SystemBC telemetry [S4].

objectives: Financial gain through ransomware and data-theft extortion; Microsoft describes double extortion (encrypting data and threatening to publish stolen information) [S1]. Sophos reports a 90/10 ransom split offered to affiliates in a recruitment advertisement on the RAMP forum [S2].

regions: North America, South America, Europe, Africa and Asia (Microsoft-observed attacks) [S1]
Check Point SystemBC victim telemetry: majority United States, then United Kingdom and Germany [S4]
targeting.notes: Sector and region list is from Microsoft observation [S1]. Check Point reports an infection profile pointing to corporate and organizational rather than consumer targets, but could not confirm whether SystemBC belongs to the Gentlemen ecosystem or was one affiliate's tool [S4]. Sophos reports 683 victim names on the leak site by the end of July 2026 [S2].

capabilities.summary: Microsoft describes a password-gated Go encryptor that escalates to SYSTEM via a scheduled task, disables Defender and adds exclusions, deletes Volume Shadow Copies, clears event logs, kills database, backup, EDR and remote-access processes, and persists via scheduled tasks and Run keys [S1]. Encryption uses per-file ephemeral Curve25519 keys with XChaCha20, a .umc16h extension and a README-GENTLEMEN.txt note [S1]. A --spread mode uses an SMB share, PsExec, WMIC, scheduled tasks, services, WinRM and PowerShell WMI, making 21 remote execution attempts per target [S1]. ESET reports the operators supply affiliates a standardized EDR-killing suite built around the in-house GentleKiller framework (at least eight variants) plus third-party BYOVD killers [S3]. Sophos reports affiliates use native Windows utilities, commercial and open-source tools and backup tampering, with ransomware deployment sometimes within 24 hours of first identified post-compromise activity [S2]. Check Point observed an affiliate attempting to deploy SystemBC proxy malware [S4].

campaigns.name: Closed-operation phase
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports the group emerged around mid-2025 as a closed ransomware operation.

campaigns.name: RaaS opened to affiliates
campaigns.summary: The group began offering The Gentlemen RaaS to affiliates; Sophos reports first leak-site victims in the same month and a 90/10 split advertisement on RAMP.

campaigns.name: SystemBC botnet telemetry (Check Point)
campaigns.summary: Check Point Research, reported via The Hacker News, found a SystemBC C2 server with over 1,570 victims after an affiliate tried to deploy the proxy malware during an incident response engagement; the leak site then listed about 320 victims.

campaigns.name: Microsoft encryptor analysis and BreachForums partnership
campaigns.summary: Microsoft published analysis of the self-propagating Go encryptor and noted a partnership with BreachForums to recruit affiliates including penetration testers and initial access brokers.

campaigns.name: ESET EDR-killer reporting
campaigns.summary: ESET, as reported by The Hacker News, described the centralized GentleKiller and BYOVD tooling provided to affiliates.

campaigns.name: Sophos GOLD SHERWOOD intrusion analysis
campaigns.summary: Sophos CTU analyzed 15 intrusions and reported 683 leak-site victims by end of July 2026.

diamond.adversary: Storm-2697 (Microsoft) / GOLD SHERWOOD (Sophos): RaaS operators plus independent affiliates [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: Go/Garble Windows encryptor with worm-like spread, Defender tampering, backup destruction, GentleKiller and BYOVD EDR killers, SystemBC in at least one affiliate case [S1][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Leak site for extortion; RAMP forum advertisement; BreachForums recruitment partnership; a SystemBC C2 server observed by Check Point [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.victim: Education, transportation, healthcare and financial organizations across multiple continents [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal profit motive with a 90/10 affiliate split; no state tasking identified in cited sources [S1][S2].
diamond.technology: Windows domain environments with SMB, WMI, WinRM and PsExec reachable, and endpoints whose EDR can be disabled by vulnerable drivers [S1][S3].

gaps: Initial access vectors are not detailed in Microsoft's analysis; initial access depends on affiliates [S1]. Secondary-site claims about FortiGate exploitation (CVE-2024-55591) and a 14,700-device inventory were not checked against a primary source and are not asserted here.

Sophos, MITRE, ESET and Check Point primary pages could not be opened (host resolution failure on direct fetch); Sophos, ESET and Check Point findings rely on search-result summaries and The Hacker News coverage. Check Point's own report was not read.
A claim that the main operator was a Russian-speaking former Qilin affiliate appeared in one search summary but was not confirmed in a second search; it is not asserted here.
A May 2026 internal data leak reportedly exposed the leader's chat logs; only ESET's reference to it was seen, and the leak itself was not reviewed [S3].
Whether SystemBC is part of the Gentlemen toolset or one affiliate's tool is unresolved per Check Point [S4].
No government attribution, indictment or sanction was found in the sources reviewed.
Leak-site victim counts differ across reporting (about 320 in April 2026 [S4]; 683 by end of July 2026 [S2]); the counts are time-dependent and unverified independently.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the Windows domain, including SMB shares, domain credentials, backup infrastructure and EDR agents, because the encryptor spreads using these and kills backup and EDR tooling [S1][S3]. Healthcare, education, transportation and financial entities are the observed victim sectors, so installation-supporting commercial and host-nation partners in those sectors are exposed [S1]. STEP 2: Affiliate-driven operations vary in access method, tempo is fast (deployment sometimes within 24 hours), and EDR killing is standardized across affiliates [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Template is affiliate access, tool staging, EDR killing (GentleKiller or BYOVD), data theft, then self-propagating encryption using PsExec, WMIC, tasks, services and WinRM [S1][S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is financially motivated extortion of civilian and contractor organizations; MDCOA is a affiliate-run encryption event against a defense contractor or host-nation critical service during a crisis, with rapid lateral spread degrading availability. Candidate indicators: vssadmin or wmic shadow deletion, wevtutil log clearing, gentlemen_system, UpdateSystem and UpdateUser tasks, GupdateS and GupdateU Run keys, a share$ hidden share, new vulnerable drivers loaded, .umc16h files, README-GENTLEMEN.txt [S1][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track leak-site and vendor reporting on victims in sectors supporting installations; shared telemetry such as the Check Point botnet data suggests public claims understate activity [S4]. (2) Authorities: criminal activity against private entities is generally a law enforcement and information-sharing matter; confirm authority before any defensive cyberspace action. (3) Mission assurance: protect offline backups, restrict PsExec, WMI and WinRM lateral movement, enable tamper protection and ASR rules as Microsoft recommends, and control loading of vulnerable drivers [S1][S3]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3 and sector partners, and coordinate with providers whose affiliates and brokers may be recruited via forums such as BreachForums and RAMP [S1][S2].

provenance.importedSummary: The Gentlemen is a group that maintains the The Gentlemen Ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS). The Gentlemen was first observed in mid-2025 who had posed The Gentlemen Ransomware as a closed ransomware and shortly later opened the ransomware as a RaaS to affiliates in September 2025. The Gentlemen has been affiliated with the threat group Storm-2697 and GOLD SHERWOOD.
